1. Demand for Money & Deposits

Q — Liquidity Preference Theory (Keynes)?

Keynes (General Theory, 1936): people hold cash for 3 motives:





Transaction motive - daily purchases (milk, vegetables).



Precautionary motive - unforeseen expenses (medical emergency).



Speculative motive - hold cash to grab a future investment opportunity ('Asset Demand of Money').

Total demand for money = transaction demand + speculative demand (NCERT omits precautionary). Cash held varies inversely with deposit interest rates.







Liquidity of assets



Examples

Cash (most liquid), gold, demand deposits, G-Sec/T-Bill, reputed shares/bonds.





Relatively illiquid



Home/real estate, paintings/sculptures.

FRBM Act 2003: Govt can't borrow from RBI (RBI can't buy govt debt in primary market) EXCEPT (i) short-term Ways & Means Advances, (ii) war/disaster/GDP fall. RBI CAN buy/sell in secondary market (OMO). Monetisation of deficit = RBI printing notes to lend to Govt (hard due to FRBM).

4. Monetary Policy — Basics

Monetary Policy = macro policy by central bank to manage money supply & interest rates -> shapes inflation, consumption, savings, investment. Milton Friedman (Nobel 1976) popularised it. Phillips Curve: inflation up = unemployment down. RBI targets 2-6% CPI (All India) via bi-monthly policy of the 6-member statutory MPC.

Q — Bond Yield relationship?

Bond yield is inversely proportional to price. Bought cheaper -> higher yield. Demand up -> price up -> yield down. Affected by: economy boom/recession, political instability, inflation, central bank action. Corporate bond rate depends on credit rating, inflation, deposit rates, G-Sec yield.

Retail Direct Scheme (2021): 'RDG account' on E-Kuber lets retail investors (incl. NRIs) buy T-Bill/G-Sec/SDL/SGB directly from RBI (Rs.0 fee, no MF commission).

Q — Operation Twist (2019-Dec)?

Special OMO: RBI buys long-term G-Sec (yield down) and sells short-term G-Sec, adjusting yields. Lower long-term G-Sec yield -> cheaper corporate bond borrowing -> more factories/jobs/GDP. NOT for inflation. First used by US Fed (1961).

Key Facts (Quick Revision)







Fact



Detail





CRR



RBI Act 1934; no legal limit; 3% (2025-Dec); no interest.





SLR



Banking Regulation Act 1949; max 40%; bank holds it itself.





Repo (Policy rate)



Decided by MPC; MSF = Repo+0.25%, SDF = Repo-0.25%.





MSF



2011; SCB/RRB against SLR-quota G-Sec; RBI can't refuse.





SDF



Urjit Patel Cmte 2013; launched 2022-Apr; no collateral; floor of corridor.





Bank Rate



= MSF since 2012; mainly for penalties.





M3



Aggregate Monetary Resources = most-used money measure.





Money multiplier



M3/M0; ~5x+ now; MM = 1/CRR (theoretical).





FRBM Act 2003



Govt can't borrow from RBI (except WMA/emergencies).





Inflation target



CPI 2-6% (4%+/-2%); set by Govt with RBI; till 31-Mar-2026.





MPC



6 members (3 RBI + 3 Govt); adopted 2016 (RBI Act Sec 45); decides only repo.





Operation Twist



2019-Dec special OMO to lower long-term G-Sec yield (US Fed 1961).





PSL



40% for SCB; 75% for RRB/SFB/UCB; applies to banks not NBFCs.
